text:
maria: heads up — canary 13B-bf16 shows a p99 uptick after yesterday's runtime change, suspect kernel selection fallback. p50 ok, p99 ~2.5x higher. :thinking:

ajay: which change? the selector heuristics? any profiler traces?

maria: yes selector. attached quick trace paste from perf_trace: 
```
2026-01-08 14:12:34.123 kernel_selector: input_seq=64, batch=8, dtype=bf16
2026-01-08 14:12:34.124 chosen_kernel=flash_hybrid_coalesce_paged
2026-01-08 14:12:34.125 fallback_kernel=fused_flash_attention
2026-01-08 14:12:34.200 kv_stride=48 bytes (unaligned to 64)
2026-01-08 14:12:34.201 latency_ms=42.8
```

maria: note the kv_stride = 48, that's coming from our interleaved layout for kv cache (pack width 6 * 8 bytes?).

sam: hmm interleaved layout + bf16 can produce 48-byte stride if packing not padded. That can trigger warp-bank conflicts on some kernels, making fused slower than paged.

ajay: do we have microbench that splits by stride alignment? can we repro locally with small harness?

maria: ran a quick microbench, results: 
```
config: 13B bf16, seq=64, batch=8
kv_layout=interleaved, stride=48 -> throughput=720 tok/s, p99=42ms
kv_layout=separate,   stride=64 -> throughput=1100 tok/s, p99=16ms
kv_layout=interleaved+pad, stride=64 -> throughput=1080 tok/s, p99=17ms
```

maria: so adding padding to reach 64 alignment recovers perf.

ajay: interesting. selector picked paged-hybrid because it expects paged wins with small seqs, but the fallback path paid penalty due to misaligned strides. Two orthogonal things: (1) kernel selection should consider stride alignment and dtype, (2) batching heuristics need to account for interleaved layout probability.

sam: agree. Also we saw a regression in fused_flash for bf16 when strides != 64 on A100 kernels in previous tests. Might be kernel bug or memory coalescing issue. Could add an alignment check into the kernel capability table.

perf-bot: Canary metrics snapshot: 
```
service=api-inference canary=13B-bf16 p99=42.8ms (baseline 16.1ms) error_rate=0.2% throughput=-8%
```

deploy-bot: Canary traffic at 5% currently. No user-facing errors.

ajay: proposed immediate mitigation: in selector, treat any kv_stride % 64 != 0 as "prefer separate layout" for fused kernels, or prefer paged variant only if stride aligned. For hotfix we can set env REDWOOD_KERNEL_STRIDE_ALIGN=64 and a flag REDWOOD_FORCE_LAYOUT_PADDING=true to pad interleaved on-the-fly.

maria: quick patch on canary: set REDWOOD_FORCE_LAYOUT_PADDING=true -> p99 back to ~17ms.

sam: good temporary fix. For long-term: (A) kernel team to investigate fused_flash bf16 coalescing; (B) selector to add stride/dtype awareness; (C) batching heuristic to factor in layout probabilities so small batches with unaligned strides pick kernels that are robust.

ajay: I'll open a PR for selector changes and add unit tests exercising stride cases. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/987 (draft)

maria: logger snippet I pushed to the PR for improved visibility: 
```
[selector] reason=layout_misaligned pref=paged stride=48 dtype=bf16 seq=64 batch=8
```

perf-bot: scheduled 24h extended canary job (stability + perf) starting now.

sam: also add regression alert if p99 > baseline * 1.5 for next 72h.

maria: thanks all — will follow up with kernel repro artifacts (nvprof traces + minimal repro harness) in the issue. :rocket:
